title: World Ecotourism in the developing courtiers

source.filename: Practice 154 IETLS 閱讀練習 - Passage 1.pdf

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The Ecotourism Society defines ecotourism as “responsible travel to natural areas which conserves the environment and improves the welfare of local people”. It is recognised as enhancing the standing of tourism because it respects natural heritage and local populations and remains within the carrying capacity of each site.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Cuba Cuba is undoubtedly an obvious site for ecotourism, with its picturesque beaches, underwater beauty, countryside landscapes, and ecological reserves. An educated population and improved infrastructure of roads and communications add to the mix. In the Caribbean region, Cuba is now the second most popular tourist destination. Ecotourism is also seen as an environmental education opportunity to heighten both visitors’ and residents’ awareness of environmental and conservation issues, and even to inspire conservation action. Ecotourism has also been credited with promoting peace, by providing opportunities for educational and cultural exchange. Tourists’ safety and health are guaranteed. Raul Castro, brother of the Cuban president, started this initiative to rescue the Cuban tradition of herbal medicine and provide natural medicines for its healthcare system. The school at Las Terrazas Eco-Tourism Community teaches herbal healthcare and children learn not only how to use medicinal herbs, but also to grow them in the school garden for teas, tinctures, ointments and creams. In Cuba, ecotourism has the potential to alleviate poverty by bringing money into the economy and creating jobs. In addition to their environmental benefits, these efforts create local employment opportunities through ecotourism.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: South America South America illustrates one potential shortcoming of ecotourism. Histoplasma capsulatum (see chapter “Histoplasmosis and HIV”), a dimorphic fungus, is the most common endemic mycosis in the United States and is associated with exposure to bat or bird droppings. Most recently, outbreaks have been reported in healthy travellers who returned from Central and South America after engaging in recreational activities associated with spelunking, adventure tourism, and ecotourism. Tourists quite often neglect sanitation while travelling. After engaging in high-risk activities, boots should be hosed off and clothing placed in airtight plastic bags for laundering. HIV-infected travellers should avoid risky behaviours or environments, such as exploring caves, particularly those that contain bat droppings.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Nowhere are a keen eye and intimate knowledge more valuable than amid this fantastic biodiversity, as travellers explore remote realms rich in wildlife. Ecotourism depends on sustainable tours that allow travellers, nature and local communities to thrive together while respecting what makes the region special. Travellers get great joy from every step they take forward on this endless but exciting journey towards sustainability. The primary threats to South America’s tropical forests are deforestation caused by agricultural expansion, cattle ranching, logging, oil extraction and spills, mining, illegal coca farming, and colonisation initiatives. Deforestation has shrunk territories belonging to indigenous peoples and wiped out more than 90 per cent of some indigenous populations. Many are taking leading roles in sustainable tourism even as they introduce protected regions to more travellers.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: East Africa In East Africa, significantly reducing illegal hunting and allowing wildlife populations to recover could generate substantial economic benefits through trophy hunting and potentially ecotourism. “Illegal hunting is an extremely inefficient use of wildlife resources because it fails to capture the value of wildlife achievable through alternative forms of use such as trophy hunting and ecotourism,” said Peter Lindsey, author of the new study. Most residents believed that ecotourism could improve this situation. Local advocates are passionate about community empowerment, love photography and write to praise current conservation efforts, raise environmental awareness and promote ecotourism.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Indonesia In Indonesia, ecotourism became an important concept in 1995 as a way to strengthen domestic travel. For local government, targeting the right markets is a prerequisite for successful ecotourism. The market for Indonesian ecotourism consists of (i) “the silent generation”, people aged 55–64 who are generally affluent and well educated, have no dependent children and can travel for four weeks; (ii) “the baby boom generation”, successful junior executives aged 35–54 who are likely to travel with their families for two to three weeks and for whom travel is a stress reliever; and (iii) “generation X”, people aged 18–29 who enjoy backpacking ecotours and are generally students able to travel for 3–12 months on a monthly budget of US$300–500. It is suggested that the promotion of Indonesian ecotourism products should aim to reach these various cohorts of tourists. The country welcomes travellers with a wide range of budgets.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: On the other hand, ecotourism provides as many services as traditional tourism. Nestled between Mexico, Guatemala and the Caribbean Sea is the country of Belize. It is a wonderful place for a Hamanasi honeymoon, offering a bottle of champagne upon arrival, three meals daily, private service on one night of your stay and a choice of adventures depending on the length of your stay. It also offers six-night and seven-night honeymoon packages. Elsewhere in the Caribbean, a variety of specially tailored tours is available, including visits to Brimstone Hill Fortress and a neighbouring island. Guided tours include rainforest, volcano and off-road plantation tours. Gregory Pereira, an extremely knowledgeable and outgoing hiking and tour guide, describes his tours: “All of our tours on St Kitts include transportation by specially modified Land Rovers, a picnic of island pastries and local fruit, fresh tropical juices, a qualified island guide and full liability insurance coverage for participants.”

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Kodai is a splendid destination for those who love being close to Mother Nature. Just as every bird sings with its own voice, every traveller can find their own route along the varied and unspoilt paths through deep valleys and steep mountains. The cheese factory here exports large quantities of cheese to countries around the world. It is located in the centre of the forest. Many travellers are attracted by the delicious cheese. This distinctive culinary experience is a popular ecotourism attraction.
